summary: [Nudge] Reminder skipped during quiet hours instead of delivered silently
description:
Steps: set quiet hours 22:00-07:00, log 7 nights with a usual bedtime of 23:00.
Expected: the 22:15 reminder is delivered silently (PR-21 item 4).
Actual: no reminder at all.
Fixed in nudge.py: quiet hours now set silent=True.

summary: [Import] No feedback while a large CSV uploads
description:
Uploading a CSV with a few hundred nights takes a couple of seconds and the page shows nothing until it reloads. Users click Import again.
Expected: a busy state on the Import button.
Actual: no change until the page reloads.

summary: [Coach] Long answers are cut off mid-sentence
description:
Asking the coach a broad question ('how do I fix my sleep schedule?') sometimes returns an answer that stops mid-sentence.
Seen with the Claude coach, not the mock.

summary: [Diary] Slept time is an hour off across the autumn clock change
description:
Night of Sat 31 Oct 2026, America/Toronto, bed 23:00, up 07:00. The clocks go back at 02:00, so the night lasted 9h.
Expected: Slept 9h 0m.
Actual: Slept 8h 0m.
Cause: durations were subtracted in local wall-clock time. Fixed: Night.duration now subtracts in UTC.

summary: [Import] Re-uploading a CSV adds the same nights again
description:
While preparing the demo I uploaded data/sample_nights.csv, then uploaded it again by mistake. The diary now lists every night twice (42 rows).
Expected: nights already in the diary are not added again.
Actual: every night is stored a second time.

summary: [Settings] Quiet hours can't end at midnight
description:
Setting quiet hours 21:00 to 00:00 is rejected with 'Invalid time'. Entering 23:59 works.
Expected: 00:00 is accepted as the end of quiet hours.

summary: [Export] CSV export writes times with +00:00 instead of the night's own UTC offset
description:
## Steps to reproduce

1. Start with an empty diary.
2. Add one night: bedtime `2026-03-01T00:25:00-05:00`, wake `2026-03-01T07:30:00-05:00`, zone `America/Toronto`.
3. Download the export (`/export`, or `Diary.export_csv()`).

## Expected

S-117 AC3: times are ISO 8601 with the UTC offset of that night's own zone, e.g.
`2026-03-01T00:25:00-05:00,2026-03-01T07:30:00-05:00,America/Toronto,`

## Actual

`2026-03-01T05:25:00+00:00,2026-03-01T12:30:00+00:00,America/Toronto,`

The instants are correct; only the offset and wall time are wrong. This also breaks AC6 (round-trip fidelity of local times).

## Evidence

`uv run python bugs/D-1-export-offset-utc/repro.py` exits 1 and prints the +00:00 row above.

## Environment

NightJar at commit 64f34e5 (S-117 first version), local run, test data only.

## Notes

Likely cause (from reading code, not fixed): `Diary.nights()` rebuilds datetimes from the UTC text in `bedtime_utc`, and `export_csv` (`src/nightjar/diary.py:75`) calls `.isoformat()` without converting to `zone(night.timezone)`.
Searches (export, UTC, CSV, offset, timezone, and phrase variants) found no duplicate. NJ-11 (Done) is related but different: duration across DST, not export format.

Reproduced 3 of 3 times. Related: NJ-11.

summary: [Export] CSV export lists nights newest first when the diary has several nights
description:
## Steps to reproduce

1. Start with an empty diary.
2. Add three nights with bedtimes 2026-03-01, 2026-03-02, 2026-03-03 (notes: first, second, third).
3. Download the export (`/export`, or `Diary.export_csv()`).

## Expected

S-117 AC4: nights in "night of" order, oldest first: first, second, third.

## Actual

Rows come out in the order third, second, first (newest first).

## Evidence

`uv run python bugs/D-2-export-order-newest-first/repro.py` prints
`export order: ['third', 'second', 'first']` and exits 1 (exits 0 once fixed).

## Environment

NightJar main at 64f34e5, local app, test data only.

## Notes

Likely cause (from reading the code, not verified by a fix): `export_csv` (`src/nightjar/diary.py:75`) iterates `self.nights()`, which is `ORDER BY bedtime_utc DESC` for the diary page. The export needs its own ascending order; `nights()` itself should stay as is because the page relies on it.

Reproduced 3 of 3 times. Related: none.
